raw_case_text:
A 33-year-old African American male patient was admitted to our hospital as a transfer from an outside hospital for further evaluation of the white blood cell (WBC) count of more than 100 K/mm. He started experiencing fever, chills, poor appetite, and 10-pound weight loss over a month before admission. He visited an outside hospital with these symptoms. Basic laboratory investigations were done which revealed the WBC count of more than 100 K/mm. His past medical history is significant for human immunodeficiency virus infection for the past 10 years. He has been noncompliant with his medications for HIV for more than 6 months. He had an appendectomy in 2003. He denied smoking cigarettes, drinking alcohol, and use of illicit drugs. He worked as a bus driver. He denied any exposure to pet animals or birds. He was afebrile on admission with blood pressure in the normal range. On examination, he had enlarged bilateral cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes. They were rubbery to touch and not tender on palpation. Absolute CD4 cell count was 847 cells/mm (reference range: 401-1532), and HIV viral load in serum was 101,591 copies/ml (reference range: not detected). Labs on admission showed that white blood cell count was 110.76 K/mm3 (reference range: 3.6-11.2 K/mm3) with 11% bands, 2% basophils, 29% blasts, 1% eosinophils, 3% lymphocytes, 7% metamyelocytes, 7% myelocytes, 9% promyelocytes, 8% monocytes, and 23% segmented neutrophils. Serum creatinine was 1.4 mg/dL (reference range: 0.7-1.3 mg/dL), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) was 14 U/L (reference range: 12-78 U/L), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) was 31 U/L (reference range: 15-37 U/L), and total bilirubin was 0.5 mg/dL (reference range: 0.2-1.0 mg/dL). He was started on intravenous fluids and allopurinol for mild acute kidney injury from tumor lysis. He was also started on a regimen of emtricitabine-tenofovir 200 mg-300 mg once daily with dolutegravir 50 mg daily for HIV. Bone marrow biopsy and aspiration were performed from the right iliac crest. Complete bone marrow evaluation with bone marrow aspiration, biopsy, and molecular and cytogenetic analysis was done, and it revealed chronic myeloid leukemia in blast crisis (35% bone marrow blasts). The cytogenetic analysis showed t(9:22) and inv(3). BCR-ABL FISH was positive. The RT-PCR was positive for coexpression of p210 and p190 fusion transcripts. He was started on intensive induction chemotherapy on hospital day 4 with cytarabine 100 mg/m, continuous intravenous infusion (CIVI) for 7 days with idarubicin 12 mg/m, and intravenous infusion (IV) for 3 days (also known as 7 + 3) along with dasatinib. At our institution, we use voriconazole for fungal prophylaxis during intensive induction chemotherapy. Due to drug interactions between dasatinib and voriconazole, the dose of dasatinib was reduced from 100 mg PO daily to 20 mg PO daily. On hospital day 16, it was noted that his total bilirubin was elevated at 1.8 mg/dL (reference range: 0.2-1.0 mg/dL), AST was elevated at 60 (reference range: 15-37 U/L), and ALT was at 41 (reference range: 12-78 U/L). Since voriconazole is metabolized through the liver, it was stopped on hospital day 16. Ultrasonogram of the liver and biliary tree was normal. On hospital day 18, dasatinib dose was increased to its normal dose of 100 mg daily. Liver function tests done on hospital day 22 showed that total bilirubin trended down to 1.0 mg/dL, AST trended down to 19 mg/dL, and ALT trended down to 24 mg/dL. Then, on hospital day 29, the patient developed new-onset tea-colored urine, fever, chills, bilateral leg pain, and muscle cramps. Blood cultures and urine cultures were negative. Repeat liver function tests showed the following results: total bilirubin was 2.3 mg/dL, AST was 1254 mg/dL, and ALT was 290 mg/dL. Serum creatine kinase was >100,000 U/L (reference range: 26-308 U/L).  Figure 1 shows the trend of CK and AST. Oral dasatinib and the patient's HIV medications emtricitabine-tenofovir 200 mg-300 mg once daily with dolutegravir 50 mg daily were discontinued.
Laboratory parameters on hospital day 29 showed pancytopenia with the hemoglobin count of 7.1 g/dL, WBC count of 0.46 K/mm, and platelet count of 23 K/mm. Chemistry showed serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 2.3 mg/dL, AST of 1254 mg/dL, and ALT of 290 mg/dL. Serum creatine kinase was >100,000 U/L (reference range: 26-308 U/L). A detailed workup for the source of sepsis was negative, including blood and urine cultures. Ultrasonogram of the liver and biliary tree was repeated, and they were normal. Urinalysis was positive for large blood but negative for red blood cells (RBCs). Urine myoglobin was elevated at 220 ng/ml (reference range: 0-13 ng/ml). Hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B DNA, hepatitis C antibody, and urine histoplasma antigen were all negative. Nasopharyngeal swab for influenza A and B PCR was negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 33-year-old African American male with HIV was transferred for evaluation of extreme leukocytosis (WBC >100 K/mm3) after 1 month of fever, chills, poor appetite, and a 10-pound weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a 10-year history of HIV and had been noncompliant with antiretroviral therapy for >6 months. Over the month preceding admission, he developed fever, chills, anorexia, and a 10-lb weight loss, and presented to an outside hospital where his WBC count was found to be >100 K/mm3.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection for 10 years (noncompliant with ART for >6 months) and appendectomy in 2003. Social/occupational history: Bus driver; denied tobacco, alcohol, illicit drugs, or pet/bird exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, anorexia, and 10-lb weight loss; on hospital day 29 developed tea-colored urine, fever, chills, bilateral leg pain, and muscle cramps.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: afebrile, normal BP. Lymphatics: enlarged, rubbery, nontender bilateral cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: WBC 110.76 K/mm3 (ref 3.6-11.2; 29% blasts, 9% promyelocytes, 7% myelocytes, 7% metamyelocytes, 11% bands, 23% segmented neutrophils, 8% monocytes, 3% lymphocytes, 2% basophils, 1% eosinophils), creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (ref 0.7-1.3), ALT 14 U/L, AST 31 U/L, total bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL. Day 16 LFTs (on voriconazole + dasatinib): total bilirubin 1.8 mg/dL, AST 60 U/L, ALT 41 U/L (normalized by day 22 after stopping voriconazole). Day 29 labs: Hb 7.1 g/dL, WBC 0.46 K/mm3, platelets 23 K/mm3, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, total bilirubin 2.3 mg/dL, AST 1,254 U/L, ALT 290 U/L, serum CK >100,000 U/L (ref 26-308 U/L), urinalysis positive for large blood without RBCs, urine myoglobin 220 ng/mL (ref 0-13 ng/mL). Negative blood/urine cultures, HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV Ab, urine Histoplasma Ag, and influenza A/B PCR. Liver/biliary ultrasound: normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunology/virology: absolute CD4 count 847 cells/mm3 (ref 401-1,532), HIV viral load 101,591 copies/mL. Right iliac crest bone marrow aspiration, biopsy, cytogenetics, FISH, and RT-PCR: chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in myeloid blast crisis (35% blasts) with t(9;22), inv(3), positive BCR-ABL FISH, and coexpression of p210 and p190 fusion transcripts.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in blast crisis with t(9;22) and inv(3) in an HIV-positive patient, complicated on hospital day 29 by severe rhabdomyolysis (CK >100,000 U/L) induced by dasatinib and/or dolutegravir-tenofovir-emtricitabine (histoplasmosis ruled out by negative urine Histoplasma antigen). Confirmation: Bone marrow biopsy/cytogenetics/RT-PCR confirming BCR-ABL1-positive CML blast crisis, and day 29 CK >100,000 U/L with myoglobinuria (220 ng/mL). Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV fluids, allopurinol, emtricitabine-tenofovir + dolutegravir, 7+3 induction chemotherapy (cytarabine + idarubicin), dasatinib, and prophylactic voriconazole (stopped day 16 for transaminitis); on day 29, dasatinib and ART were discontinued due to severe rhabdomyolysis.
